chunks: Abi (may Allah have mercy on him) from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Uthman from a man from Hafs ibn Ghiyath who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say to a man: 'Do you love remaining in the world?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'And why?' He said: 'For reciting Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad.' So he fell silent about him. Then he said after a while: 'O Hafs! Whoever dies from our Shias and does not recite the Quran well, will be taught in his grave so that Allah raises his rank through it. Indeed, the ranks of Paradise are according to the number of verses of the Quran. So it is said to the reciter of the Quran: 'Recite and ascend.'

key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ: Qul Huwa Allahu (Surah al-Ikhlas, the chapter of 'Say, He is Allah')

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting the Quran in the grave and how does it affect one's rank in Paradise?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Thawab al-Amal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the profound spiritual merit of Surah al-Ikhlas, noting that even those who did not master Quranic recitation in life will be taught in the grave to elevate their status. This teaching underscores the Shia belief in the intercessory and elevating power of Quranic knowledge, where each verse recited corresponds to ascending a level in Paradise, reflecting the verse 'Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Quran that you might understand.'

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 10. Abi (rah) from Muhammad b. Yahya al-’Attar from Muhammad b. Ahmad from al-Hassan b. Ali b. Abi Uthman from a man from Hafs b. Ghiyath who said:

“O Hafs! One from our Shias who dies without having a good knowledge of recitation of the Holy Quran, is taught the Holy Quran in grave so that Allah grants him great ranks. Know that the levels of Paradise are equal to the number of verses in the Holy Quran. A reciter of the Holy Quran is told over there, ‘Recite a verse of the Holy Quran and go to the next level’.”
